scope: Round 2 additions and sharpened novelty boundaries; primary original papers and official metadata. Read depth is deliberately explicit. No performance figures from secondary summaries are used.

sources.title: SLIM: A Heterogeneous Accelerator for Edge Inference of Sparse Large Language Model via Adaptive Thresholding
sources.read_depth: Original sections 5.4, 6.1-6.3, 7.1, 7.6 and Table 2 read; remaining sections inspected selectively.
sources.evidence: Input SRAM holds B*L*embedding_dim inputs, with L=1 for decode; corresponding NAND weights are fetched once. Die-level PE has 16 MACs and 64KB SRAM at 1GHz. Fused FFN vectors are page aligned and distributed evenly over dies. Multi-plane read is explicitly not implemented.
sources.relevance: Direct prior against claiming read-once multi-input in-flash execution or fused gate/up/down placement as new.
sources.hardware_limits: Custom die/channel ASIC, finite input/output SRAM; synthesis/simulation rather than fabricated NAND compute. Dense and MoE models; approximate neuron sparsity must be disabled for exact-routing comparison.
sources.code: Author account contains https://github.com/wh-xu/sparse-ffn-llm (MIT, README usage TODO), an approximate FFN/MoE software implementation; no explicit SLIM hardware artifact association verified.

sources.title: RecFlash: Fast Recommendation Inference on NAND Flash-Based In-Storage Computing with Embedding-Optimized Data Mapping
sources.venue: Extended preprint of APCCAS 2025 conference work
sources.read_depth: Original sections III-IV read, including page caching, frequency mapping, and hardware evaluation methodology.
sources.evidence: Co-locates hot small embeddings in NAND pages, distributes hot pages across planes, and adds a 128KiB controller SRAM page cache. Cache area is estimated as 0.44mm2 at 28nm.
sources.relevance: Prior for flash frequency-aware page locality combined with plane parallelism and finite SRAM page reuse.
sources.hardware_limits: Controller page cache for small embedding lookups, not die-local expert GEMV replay. Modeling includes NAND-PIM assumptions; cannot transfer its speedup to AiF.

sources.title: FLINT: Efficiently Leveraging High Bandwidth Flash for Capacity-Scalable LLM Inference Acceleration
sources.venue: arXiv preprint; peer-reviewed venue not verified
sources.read_depth: Original sections 4.1-4.4, 5, 6.2-6.3, and related-work section read; introduction and background inspected.
sources.evidence: Dynamic burst controller coalesces requests and pipelines reads through existing page/cache latches. All-plane bursts share block/page coordinates. Phantom-plane refresh adds one plane per die and independent program resources. Corrected foreground pages are copied into the offline plane with migration bitmaps and program queues.
sources.relevance: Close prior for buffer-aware flash coalescing and keeping background refresh off the inference path.
sources.hardware_limits: HBF GPU memory tier, no in-flash compute. Extra plane/copy and program-circuit independence violate strict unchanged-capacity one-copy assumptions. HBF timing and endurance are modeled.
sources.code: In-house trace-driven simulator; no author public artifact verified.

sources.title: FlashAccel: Leveraging High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) for High-Throughput LLM Inference
sources.venue: arXiv preprint; peer-reviewed venue not verified
sources.read_depth: Original sections III-B, IV, V-A/V-B and memory interfaces read; evaluation inspected selectively.
sources.evidence: Planes are coupled into megaplanes sharing command control and same block/page offsets. Static weights are chunked into megapages, striped round robin in execution order, and packed across operator boundaries. Megaplane size trades load balance against HBM buffering. KV stragglers use selective HBM replication.
sources.relevance: Strong prior for execution-order placement, coupled flash group granularity, and buffer/load-balance co-design.
sources.hardware_limits: GPU/HBM/HBF system with SRAM caches, 96 planes/die, SLC, hyperpage transfers. Selective replication is stated for KV, not expert weight replicas. Not ordinary 4-plane AiF GEMV.
sources.code: No author public implementation verified; HBFSim is an independent project, not this paper's artifact.

sources.title: PiF: In-Flash Acceleration for Data-Intensive Applications
sources.read_depth: Original introduction and sections 2-3 hardware/ECC/pipelining read; not an exhaustive evaluation audit.
sources.evidence: CoX puts digital accelerator and weak ECC under NAND arrays. Page/cache latches overlap sensing with processing; ECC and pattern matching also pipeline by subpage. Strong controller ECC is a fallback.
sources.relevance: Underlying digital in-flash buffering and ECC pipeline prior, not evidence of expert multi-request scheduling.
sources.hardware_limits: Pattern matching rather than GEMV. Prototype emulates enhanced NAND on OpenSSD; area and compute costs are workload specific.
sources.code: Uses OpenROAD, OpenRAM and OpenSSD; paper-specific public source not verified.

sources.title: DIAMoND: Dynamic Inference for Adaptive Edge MOE with Heterogeneous In-NAND and Near-DRAM Compute Architecture
sources.read_depth: Official abstract/metadata only. No legal author preprint located in bounded author/arXiv/GitHub searches. ResearchGate explicitly has no full text.
sources.evidence: Abstract states mask-based mapping and heterogeneous in-NAND/near-DRAM computation. Detailed placement and execution mechanism remain unknown.
sources.relevance: Unresolved close prior; cannot clear a novelty claim about adaptive MoE mapping.
sources.hardware_limits: CR dependence, replicas, plane independence, precision, and SRAM contexts not verified.

sources.title: Cambricon-FlexLLM: A Flexible Chiplet-Based Hybrid Architecture for On-Device 70B LLM Inference
sources.read_depth: Official metadata and author-written Kudos description only; official full/PDF/epdf inaccessible. OpenAlex marks diamond OA/CC-BY but no repository full text; no author preprint located.
sources.evidence: Author description mentions grouping often-used-together data, weight reordering, and sparsity-aware partitioning. Exact algorithm not read.
sources.relevance: Unresolved close prior for learned coactivation or workload-adaptive placement.
sources.hardware_limits: Cannot infer replica, CR, projection, replay, or plane-context assumptions from the abstract/summary.

sources.title: Distributed Matrix-Vector Multiplication: A Convolutional Coding Approach
sources.read_depth: Original first-page systematic sum-parity example, introduction and coding motivation read; not a complete scheme/evaluation audit.
sources.evidence: Explicitly distributes A0*x, A1*x and (A0+A1)*x and reconstructs from any two; attributes this baseline to earlier coded computing work. Develops low-complexity coding beyond it.
sources.relevance: Direct prior against claiming sum-parity row-block matvec recovery as new.
sources.hardware_limits: Distributed workers, real arithmetic; no NAND page layout, INT8 width, or hardware constraints.
sources.code: No repository verified for this paper.

sources.title: RAIL: Predictable, Low Tail Latency for NVMe Flash
sources.read_depth: Original sections 2-4 and 6 selected hardware/placement/serialization details read; no full evaluation reproduction.
sources.evidence: Places XOR data/parity stride elements on different LUNs and reconstructs a read blocked by long writes/erases from other elements. Enforces at most one high-latency LUN per stride; tunes stride/capacity/bandwidth. Real Linux LightNVM/PBLK implementation.
sources.relevance: Direct NAND prior for parity placement and avoiding known background blocking.
sources.hardware_limits: Reconstructs data bytes, not GEMV outputs; write throttling and read amplification matter. Does not establish in-flash integer coding.
sources.code: Paper reports 1618 added C lines in PBLK and extensive validation. Public paper-specific repo not yet verified.

sources.title: Tiny-Tail Flash: Near-Perfect Elimination of Garbage Collection Tail Latencies in NAND SSDs
sources.read_depth: Official abstract and original selected design/constraint excerpts; full evaluation not audited.
sources.evidence: Uses RAIN reconstruction to bypass GC-blocked reads, rotating GC to restrict simultaneous blocked planes, and capacitor-backed buffering. Depends on intra-plane copyback.
sources.relevance: Older close prior for parity avoiding flash maintenance tails.
sources.hardware_limits: GC management and byte reconstruction; simulation and copyback assumptions differ from AiF.

sources.title: TR-ABFT: Tile-Resilient Fault Detection for Neural Processing Units
sources.read_depth: Official abstract and Crossref metadata; original paper text section 3.2.1 and limitations read through public ResearchGate search indexing. Official HTML/PDF returned 429/403. Not full-paper audit.
sources.evidence: Checksum decomposition explicitly uses b=256*bH+bL; bL=((b+128) mod 256)-128 and bH=(b-bL)/256, then computes two INT8 check tiles. Alternative modulo-239 checks. Targets fault detection with unchanged PE topology.
sources.relevance: Direct prior for the exact signed-radix-256 checksum representation on ordinary INT8 PEs.
sources.hardware_limits: NPU error detection, not missing NAND-chip output repair or tail-latency scheduling. Simulator/operator shape estimates, not radiation-tested silicon.

sources.title: Coded Access Architectures for Dense Memory Systems
sources.venue: Proceedings of FTC 2020, Volume 2; author PDF version date unspecified
sources.read_depth: Original abstract/introduction and structure of architecture read; not full controller or evaluation audit.
sources.evidence: Dedicated parity banks provide alternate read paths and schedules around memory-bank contention using multi-bank Reed-Solomon coding.
sources.relevance: Prior for physical parity placement to expand scheduling alternatives; does not imply NAND applicability.
sources.hardware_limits: DDR/HBM/HMC and Ramulator, not NAND or in-flash GEMV.
